hero.eyebrow: The Linden House · bed and breakfast, York
hero.title: Six rooms,
hero.lede: A Georgian townhouse inside the city walls, with six quiet rooms and a breakfast worth getting up for. Scroll through a night here, from the lamp by the door to the last cup of tea.

stages.c: The lamp's on by the door. Ring the bell, or let yourself in with the code we sent.
A key on a brass tag, a map with our favourite places marked, and a cup of tea if you want one.
Up two flights to the Linden Room. Bed turned down, curtains drawn, a little chocolate on the pillow.
Thick walls, blackout curtains, no traffic. The house goes quiet by eleven.
Eggs from the farm up the road, bread baked at dawn, and as much coffee as you like.
Bags can stay with us until six. The Minster is eight minutes on foot.

rooms.title: Six rooms,
rooms.sub: Every room has its own bathroom, a proper mattress, blackout curtains and a tray with good tea. Pick one to see the dates.

list.d: Ground-floor calm, French doors onto the garden.
A view along the city walls from the window seat.
Our biggest, with a roll-top bath and the bells.
Looks into the old linden tree. Quietest in the house.
Beams, skylights and a lot of stairs. Worth it.
A snug single for solo travellers.

dates.title: Pick your nights,
dates.sub: Prices are per room per night, breakfast for two included. Weekends are two nights minimum.

nearby.title: Leave the car,
nearby.sub: The house sits just inside the walls. Everything worth seeing is a short walk away, and we'll point you to the good stuff.

places.d: Climb the 275 steps of the central tower.
The crooked medieval street, best before ten.
Tea rooms since 1937. Worth the queue.
